title: Adding a White Photo Border? Count It Inside the Paper Size
description: Calculate the image area inside a white photo border, check the inner crop in millimeters and verify the printed result before ordering a full batch.
direct: A white border uses space inside the chosen paper size. Subtract the left and right borders from the width and the top and bottom borders from the height.
figureAlt: A portrait print with a five-millimeter white border illustrates a 90 by 140 millimeter photo inside 100 by 150 millimeter paper.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export.
cards.choice.heading: Start with the decision
cards.choice.body: For a 100 × 150 mm sheet with a 5 mm border on every side, the inner image area is 90 × 140 mm. That is a different shape from the paper, so a crop prepared for the full sheet may need another check.
sections.detail-0.heading: Paper size is the outer size
sections.detail-0.body: At 300 DPI, millimeters convert to pixels using mm ÷ 25.4 × 300. Rounding to whole pixels is normal. Resampling cannot create genuine scene detail. A lab may apply its own fit, fill or borderless enlargement, so tell it that the white margin is already included in your delivered file.
sections.detail-1.heading: Check what reaches paper
sections.detail-1.body: It supports paper size, DPI, millimeter borders, crop review and exported-dimension reports. Print-size fitting is an advanced feature, with three successful advanced exports free. Printer scaling and physical trimming remain outside the app’s control. The illustration is a conceptual border example, not a calibrated ruler.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: On 100 × 150 mm paper, what does a 5 mm border on each edge leave?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: It leaves a 90 × 140 mm image area. Check that shape and the crop as well as the total paper size.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Why did my white margins print narrower than planned?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Check whether the printer or lab enlarged the image to fill the paper. Measure a test print and confirm its scaling settings.

steps.step-1.text: In DPI: Photo Print Prep, set the actual paper dimensions, target DPI and white border in millimeters.
steps.step-2.text: Review the crop for the inner image area. Keep faces and important edges away from the border and confirm there are enough source pixels for the chosen output.
steps.step-3.text: Export and read the verification report. Make a proof and check the print settings before sending the full batch to a printer or lab.
